Apple___Apple_scab.description: Fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis. Produces olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and fruit.
treatments: Apply Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/L at bud break
Use Captan 50 WP as protective spray
Remove and destroy fallen infected leaves
prevention: Ensure proper air circulation by pruning
Apple___Apple_scab.organic_remedy: Spray neem oil (5ml/L) at early stages. Apply compost tea as foliar spray for prevention.

Apple___Black_rot.description: Caused by Botryosphaeria obtusa. Produces brown lesions with concentric rings on leaves and fruit.
treatments: Prune and burn infected branches immediately
prevention: Maintain tree vigor with balanced fertilization
Apple___Black_rot.organic_remedy: Apply Bordeaux mixture (1%) as preventive spray during dormant season.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: Caused by Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae. Yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surface with tube-like structures below.
treatments: Apply Myclobutanil fungicide at pink bud stage
Remove nearby cedar/juniper trees if possible
prevention: Remove galls from cedar trees in early spring
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.organic_remedy: Spray sulfur-based fungicide at early infection stage.

Apple___healthy.description: No disease detected. The apple leaf appears healthy.

Blueberry___healthy.description: No disease detected. The blueberry plant appears healthy.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: Caused by Podosphaera clandestina. White powdery coating on leaves, shoots, and sometimes fruit.
prevention: Ensure adequate spacing for air flow
Water at base, avoid wetting foliage
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.organic_remedy: Spray milk solution (1:9 milk to water) or baking soda (5g/L) weekly.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: No disease detected. The cherry leaf appears healthy.
prevention: Monitor for early signs of disease

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis. Rectangular gray-brown lesions running parallel to leaf veins.
treatments: Practice crop rotation with non-host crops
prevention: Plow under crop residues after harvest
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.organic_remedy: Apply Trichoderma viride (5g/L) as foliar spray.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Caused by Puccinia sorghi. Small, circular to elongate brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.
treatments: Use Propiconazole 25 EC @ 1ml/L for severe cases
prevention: Early sowing to avoid peak disease period
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.organic_remedy: Neem oil spray (5ml/L) at early infection. Ensure good plant nutrition with compost.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Caused by Exserohilum turcicum. Long, elliptical gray-green lesions (2-15 cm) on leaves.
treatments: Apply Propiconazole 25 EC @ 1ml/L at first symptoms
Destroy infected crop residues after harvest
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.organic_remedy: Spray cow urine (10% solution) mixed with neem oil.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: No disease detected. The corn plant appears healthy.

Grape___Black_rot.description: Caused by Guignardia bidwellii. Brown circular lesions with dark margins on leaves; berries shrivel and turn black.
prevention: Prune vines for good air circulation
Grape___Black_rot.organic_remedy: Bordeaux mixture (1%) spray at 15-day intervals during growing season.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: Complex fungal disease involving Phaeomoniella and Phaeoacremonium species. Tiger-stripe pattern on leaves; dark spots on berries.
treatments: No complete cure exists — manage by pruning infected wood
prevention: Remove and burn severely infected vines
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).organic_remedy: Apply Trichoderma harzianum paste on pruning wounds.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Caused by Isariopsis clavispora. Brownish-black spots with yellow halos on leaves, primarily on lower canopy.
prevention: Ensure good air circulation through trellising

Grape___healthy.description: No disease detected. The grape leaf appears healthy.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: Bacterial disease spread by Asian citrus psyllid. Causes asymmetric yellow mottling, small lopsided fruit, and eventual tree decline.
treatments: No cure available — manage psyllid vector with Imidacloprid
Apply balanced nutrition (micronutrients) to prolong tree life
Remove severely affected trees to prevent spread
prevention: Control psyllid population with systemic insecticides
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).organic_remedy: Use neem-based insecticides for psyllid control. Apply foliar micro-nutrients (Zn, Mn, Fe).

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Caused by Xanthomonas arboricola. Small, angular, water-soaked spots on leaves that become necrotic.
treatments: Prune infected twigs in dry weather
Peach___Bacterial_spot.organic_remedy: Bordeaux mixture (0.5%) spray at leaf fall and pre-bloom.

Peach___healthy.description: No disease detected. The peach leaf appears healthy.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Caused by Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria. Water-soaked spots on leaves and raised bumpy lesions on fruit.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.organic_remedy: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L) as biocontrol agent.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: No disease detected. The bell pepper plant appears healthy.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Caused by Alternaria solani. Dark brown concentric ring (target-like) lesions on lower/older leaves first.
treatments: Apply Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/L at first symptoms
Potato___Early_blight.organic_remedy: Spray Trichoderma viride (5g/L) preventively. Apply compost tea foliar spray.

Potato___Late_blight.description: Caused by Phytophthora infestans. Water-soaked dark lesions on leaves; white fungal growth on underside in humid conditions. Can destroy entire crop in days.
treatments: Destroy all infected plant material by burning
prevention: Hill up soil around plants to protect tubers
Monitor weather — spray preventively before humid spells
Potato___Late_blight.organic_remedy: Bordeaux mixture (1%) spray at 7-day intervals during humid weather.

Potato___healthy.description: No disease detected. The potato plant appears healthy.

Raspberry___healthy.description: No disease detected. The raspberry plant appears healthy.

Soybean___healthy.description: No disease detected. The soybean plant appears healthy.
prevention: Use inoculated seed for nitrogen fixation

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: Caused by Podosphaera xanthii. White powdery growth on upper and lower leaf surfaces. Reduces photosynthesis and yield.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.organic_remedy: Milk spray (1:9 ratio with water) applied weekly. Baking soda (5g/L) + liquid soap.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: Caused by Diplocarpon earlianum. Dark purple spots on leaves that coalesce into large scorched areas.
prevention: Maintain proper plant spacing and bed hygiene
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.organic_remedy: Spray neem oil (5ml/L). Apply compost mulch to prevent soil splash.

Strawberry___healthy.description: No disease detected. The strawberry plant appears healthy.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Caused by Xanthomonas species. Small, dark, greasy-looking spots on leaves; raised scabby spots on fruit.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Caused by Alternaria solani. Dark brown target-shaped (concentric ring) lesions starting from lower leaves.
treatments: Remove lower infected leaves and destroy
Tomato___Early_blight.organic_remedy: Trichoderma viride (5g/L) preventive spray. Neem oil (5ml/L) at early stages.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Caused by Phytophthora infestans. Large dark water-soaked patches on leaves; white mold on underside. Can collapse entire crop rapidly.
treatments: Remove all infected plants and burn
Tomato___Late_blight.organic_remedy: Bordeaux mixture (1%) spray every 7 days during humid weather. Remove lower foliage.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Caused by Passalora fulva. Yellow patches on upper leaf surface with olive-green velvety mold underneath.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.organic_remedy: Improve air flow. Spray baking soda solution (5g/L) with few drops of liquid soap.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Caused by Septoria lycopersici. Numerous small circular spots with dark borders and gray centers on lower leaves.
treatments: Use Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5g/L at weekly intervals
Remove and destroy infected lower leaves
prevention: Mulch heavily to prevent soil splash
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.organic_remedy: Copper-based organic fungicide. Remove affected leaves. Apply neem cake to soil.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Caused by Tetranychus urticae. Tiny yellow dots on leaves; fine webbing on undersides. Leaves turn bronze and dry out.
prevention: Avoid water stress — mites thrive on stressed plants
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.organic_remedy: Strong water spray to dislodge mites. Neem oil (5ml/L) spray on leaf undersides. Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis).

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Caused by Corynespora cassiicola. Brown lesions with concentric zonation on leaves, stems, and fruit.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Viral disease spread by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). Upward leaf curling, yellowing, stunted growth, poor fruit set.
treatments: No cure for viral infection — control whitefly vector
Apply Imidacloprid 17.8 SL @ 0.3ml/L to control whiteflies
Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
prevention: Install yellow sticky traps for whitefly monitoring
Use silver/UV-reflective mulch to repel whiteflies
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.organic_remedy: Neem oil (5ml/L) for whitefly control. Yellow sticky traps. Remove infected plants promptly.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Viral disease causing light/dark green mosaic pattern on leaves, leaf distortion, and reduced fruit quality. Spread by contact.
treatments: No chemical cure — remove infected plants
Disinfect tools with 10% bleach between plants
Wash hands with soap after handling infected material
prevention: Avoid tobacco products near tomato fields
Handle healthy plants before infected ones
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.organic_remedy: Spray milk solution (1:9) on tools and plants to reduce virus spread. Remove infected plants.

Tomato___healthy.description: No disease detected. The tomato plant appears healthy.
